name: linux-trail
description: Master Linux fundamentals through 10 progressive challenges in a shared environment.

challenges.name: bash-history
challenges.description: Inspect past terminal command execution records.

flags.description: Find the flag in the command execution history.
hints: Check the `.bash_history` file in your home directory.
Run the `history` command to see previously executed commands.

flags.description: Find the second flag embedded in the history timestamps.
hints: History entries may contain timestamps.
Inspect `~/.bash_history` carefully for hidden data.

challenges.name: cat-reading
challenges.description: Read file contents in the terminal using standard utilities.

flags.description: Print the contents of the flag file to reveal the secret.
hints: Use the `cat` command to read file contents.
The target file is `flag.txt` in the challenge directory.

flags.description: Use a pager to read the same file.
hints: Try `less flag.txt` or `more flag.txt`.
Pagers are useful for viewing file contents page by page.

challenges.name: env-vars
challenges.description: Read settings and flags configured via environment variables.

hints: Run the `env` or `printenv` commands.
Search for the variable names matching 'SECRET_FLAG'.

challenges.name: file-listing
challenges.description: Learn to list all files in a directory, including hidden dotfiles.

flags.description: Find the hidden flag file in the challenge directory.
hints: Use `ls -la` to list all files, including hidden ones.
Files starting with a dot are hidden in Linux.

flags.description: Find the second hidden flag using glob patterns.
hints: Try `echo .*` to see hidden files.
Use `find` with `-name '.*'` to locate all dotfiles.

challenges.name: find-search
challenges.description: Search the directory tree for files matching specific names.

flags.description: Locate the file named secret_flag.txt in the directory structure.
hints: Use the `find` command to search recursively.
Run `find /opt/challenges/find-search -name 'secret_flag.txt'`.

flags.description: Find all flag files in the challenge directory tree.
hints: Use `find` with `-name '*flag*'` to match multiple files.
Combine `find` with `xargs` or `-exec`.

challenges.name: grep-pattern
challenges.description: Filter and search log files for specific patterns.

flags.description: Find the flag matching the string 'flag' inside the log file.
hints: Use the `grep` command to search for matching text.
Run `grep flag /opt/challenges/grep-pattern/access.log`.

flags.description: Find the flag with surrounding context lines.
hints: Use `grep -C 2 flag access.log` to see context.
Context helps confirm you found the right line.

challenges.name: network-check
challenges.description: Interact with network socket interfaces on the local loopback.

flags.description: Talk to the local HTTP server running on port 8080.
hints: Use `curl` or `nc` to connect to localhost.

flags.description: Discover the service running on port 8080 without connecting.
hints: Use `ss` or `netstat` to list listening ports.
Try `ss -tlnp` to see TCP listeners.

challenges.name: perm-check
challenges.description: Practice executing files without having directory read access.

flags.description: Access the flag.txt file inside a directory you cannot list.
hints: Directory read permission (`r`) allows listing files. Execute (`x`) allows traversing it.
You cannot list `/opt/challenges/perm-check/restricted/` but you can access `/opt/challenges/perm-check/restricted/flag.txt` directly if you know the name.

challenges.name: proc-inspect
challenges.description: Inspect running system processes and their command line options.

flags.description: Find the secret flag in the arguments of a running process.
hints: Use the `ps` command to inspect running processes.
Run `ps aux` or `ps -ef` to see command line arguments.

flags.description: Find the PID of the secret process and inspect it.
hints: Use `pgrep` to find the process ID by name.
Run `pgrep -f secret-agent` to find the PID.

challenges.name: tar-extract
challenges.description: Decompress tarballs and zip files in the terminal.

flags.description: Decompress the challenge tar archive to read the flag.
hints: Use the `tar` utility to decompress archives.
Run `tar -xf /opt/challenges/tar-extract/archive.tar.gz -C /tmp` and read the flag file.

flags.description: List the contents of the archive without extracting.
hints: Use `tar -tzf archive.tar.gz` to list contents.
The `t` flag lists contents, `z` handles gzip, `f` specifies file.
